topic: Cardiovascular risk assessment in primary care

audits.title: Deprivation and systematic stroke prevention in general practice: an audit among general practitioners in the Rotterdam region, The Netherlands.
audits.standard: Guideline-based review criteria judged by an expert panel
audits.setting: General practices in the Rotterdam region

cycle1.result: Patients in deprived neighbourhoods had higher risk of suboptimal preventive care (OR 1.95, 95% CI 0.98-3.90); women OR 3.57 (1.39-9.16).

audits.other_findings: Suboptimal care was mainly poor follow-up of treated hypertension and diabetes and missed cardiovascular risk assessment.
audits.citation: de Koning JS, Klazinga N, Koudstaal PJ, Prins A, Borsboom GJ, Peeters A, et al.. Deprivation and systematic stroke prevention in general practice: an audit among general practitioners in the Rotterdam region, The Netherlands. Eur J Public Health. 2003;13(4):340-346. doi:10.1093/eurpub/13.4.340. PMID: 14703321.

audits.title: Quality of care in stroke prevention: results of an audit study among general practitioners.
audits.standard: Guideline-based review criteria judged by a GP and neurologist panel
audits.setting: 77 GPs of patients from two stroke referral hospitals, Rotterdam

cycle1.result: Suboptimal care in 44% of cases (31% possibly or likely failing to prevent stroke); 52% of shortcomings were inadequate hypertension control.

audits.other_findings: 17% of shortcomings concerned inadequate cardiovascular risk assessment.
audits.citation: de Koning JS, Klazinga NS, Koudstaal PJ, Prins A, Dippel DW, Heeringa J, et al.. Quality of care in stroke prevention: results of an audit study among general practitioners. Prev Med. 2004;38(2):129-136. doi:10.1016/j.ypmed.2003.09.018. PMID: 14715204.

audits.title: [Implementation of clinical guidelines in general practice. The effect of journal audit and continuing education for the treatment of cardiovascular risk factors in patients with and without type 2 diabetes].
audits.standard: Clinical guidelines for prevention of ischaemic heart disease in hypertension, dyslipidaemia and type 2 diabetes

cycle1.result: Approximately 15-40% of patients achieved treatment goals.

audits.intervention: GP education through workshops and an international meeting, plus journal audit.

cycle2.result: Some improvement; gap between recommended and actual treatment remained.

audits.other_findings: Second sample was a new patient population collected by 170 GPs.
audits.citation: Madsbad S, Larsen ML, Adeler HF, Kryhlmand M, Westergaard M. [Implementation of clinical guidelines in general practice. The effect of journal audit and continuing education for the treatment of cardiovascular risk factors in patients with and without type 2 diabetes]. Ugeskr Laeger. 2006;168(17):1640-1645. PMID: 16674875.

audits.title: An educational intervention, involving feedback of routinely collected computer data, to improve cardiovascular disease management in UK primary care.
audits.standard: Evidence-based audit criteria for cardiovascular disease, e.g. cholesterol management in ischaemic heart disease
audits.setting: UK general practices in a cardiovascular data feedback programme (St George's, University of London)

cycle1.result: Cholesterol recording 47.6%; mean cholesterol 5.18 mmol/L; statin prescribing 46%; recorded IHD prevalence 3.8%.

audits.intervention: Educational feedback of routinely collected computer data with peer-led learning, inter-practice comparisons and lists of patients needing intervention.

cycle2.result: After three iterations: cholesterol recording 89.0%; mean cholesterol 4.67 mmol/L; statin prescribing 68% (via 57%); recorded IHD prevalence 4.0%.

audits.other_findings: Eight years of the programme; the approach was also applied to atrial fibrillation, heart failure and renal disease.
audits.citation: de Lusignan S. An educational intervention, involving feedback of routinely collected computer data, to improve cardiovascular disease management in UK primary care. Methods Inf Med. 2007;46(1):57-62. doi:10.1055/s-0038-1628133. PMID: 17224982.

audits.title: Audit on cardiovascular disease preventive care in general practice.
audits.standard: Agreed criteria and standards for cardiovascular disease preventive care (ten indicators)

cycle1.result: Targets achieved in 3 of 10 indicators: blood pressure recording 92.4%, blood sugar screening 72.7%, latest BP ≤140/90 mmHg in hypertensives 71.3%. Other indicators ranged from 11.1% to 66.7% (hypertension and diabetes registers, smoking status, height and weight, lipid screening, glycaemic targets in diabetics).

audits.other_findings: Vast differences between individual clinics. Patients aged 45 years and above.
audits.citation: Chan SC, Lee TW, Teoh LC, Abdullah ZC, Xavier G, Sim CK, et al.. Audit on cardiovascular disease preventive care in general practice. Singapore Med J. 2008;49(4):311-315. PMID: 18418523.

audits.title: Cardiovascular risk assessment: audit findings from a nurse clinic--a quality improvement initiative.
audits.setting: Nurse CVD risk assessment clinic, Northland general practice

cycle1.result: 430 (69.2%) had 5-year risk < 15%; 84 (13.5%) > 15%; anti-platelet prescribing for risk > 15% 71%, lipid lowering 65%.

cycle2.result: Anti-platelet prescribing rose to 86% and lipid lowering to 72%; 34 showed improved CVD risk.

audits.other_findings: 71% of the eligible population had an initial CVD risk assessment.
audits.citation: Waldron S, Horsburgh M. Cardiovascular risk assessment: audit findings from a nurse clinic--a quality improvement initiative. J Prim Health Care. 2009;1(3):226-231. doi:10.1071/hc09226. PMID: 20690387.

audits.title: [Cardiovascular risk factors. An audit of their detection in primary care].
audits.standard: Recording of preventive cardiovascular activities (target not reported)
audits.setting: Primary care centre (CAP La Mina, Sant Adrià de Besós)

cycle1.result: Blood pressure measurement 45%, cholesterol 23%, height and weight 8%, smoking enquiry 40%; risk factors recorded in clinical history 87%, age and sex card 72%.

audits.intervention: Corrective measures following medical audit methodology (details not reported).

cycle2.result: Blood pressure 79%, cholesterol 76%, height and weight 71%, smoking enquiry 56%; recording 98% in clinical history and 91% in age and sex card.

audits.other_findings: Audit prompted by low recorded prevalence of hypertension, hypercholesterolaemia, obesity and smoking.
audits.citation: Benet Martí JM, Cortés Vargas P, Solé Villa J, Guarga Rojas A, Marquet Palomer R, Muñoz Grimaldo M, et al.. [Cardiovascular risk factors. An audit of their detection in primary care]. Aten Primaria. 1990;7 Spec No:20-2, 24-6, 28. PMID: 2104168.

audits.title: The quality of cardiovascular disease prevention in rural primary care.
audits.standard: Recording of cardiovascular risk factors and lifestyle advice for high-risk patients and those with cardiovascular disease

cycle1.result: High-risk vs diagnosed: blood pressure recorded 94% vs 99% (P = 0.019); physical activity 24% vs 56%; dietary advice 32% vs 51% (P = 0.001); physical activity advice 34% vs 56%.

audits.other_findings: Recording of risk factors was positively associated with practice involvement in quality improvement.
audits.citation: Allenby A, Kinsman L, Tham R, Symons J, Jones M, Campbell S. The quality of cardiovascular disease prevention in rural primary care. Aust J Rural Health. 2016;24(2):92-98. doi:10.1111/ajr.12224. PMID: 26255899.
